Alex — great question, and glad Horizon liked the demo. I pulled together a concise comparison and attached a one-pager that highlights the trade-offs for a short pilot vs a longer committed contract. Summary highlights below (high level):

- Billing/invoicing: Marketplace = single billing through AWS with consolidated invoice lines; Redwood still receives payout via marketplace but we cannot issue a Redwood invoice to your AP for the same seat/subscription. Direct = Redwood issues monthly invoice or PO-based invoicing to your finance team.
- Credits & co-sell: Marketplace listing enables marketplace partner incentives on the AWS side (co-sell credits, listing-level incentives), but those incentives are typically realized by cloud partner teams and may require co-sell registration. Direct deals can include negotiated discounts/credits in the order form.
- Compliance & MSA: Marketplace purchases reference the marketplace terms; for many enterprises that is sufficient for pilots. For SOC 2 and strict data residency clauses (e.g., addenda with controls), we typically use a direct MSA or a marketplace listing + a signed attachment (Redwood MSA highlighted). The paperwork differs slightly but both are workable.

Attached: redwood_marketplace_vs_direct_onepager.pdf (one-pager), draft MSA highlights doc for reference.

Hi Alex/Sarah — quick notes from partnerships/finance: 

1) Migration path: Marketplace -> Direct is common. Best practice: start on Marketplace for speed, then execute a direct order form when you convert. We generally do NOT issue retroactive invoices for marketplace-subscription months; instead we provide an outbound credit or an order-level pro-rate on the new direct contract to align economics. That keeps audit trails clean.

2) Co-sell & incentives: To access AWS co-sell incentives, we need Horizon to register the opportunity in the AWS partner portal and authorize Redwood to submit the co-sell request. Timing: co-sell approval can take 2–4 weeks and is typically a post-sales process. Co-sell incentives are applied to partner/ISV sales teams and do not change Horizon's invoice directly. If Horizon wants a pass-through discount on the customer invoice, that must be negotiated into a direct order form.

3) Support/onboarding: No SLA delta for pilot customers based on procurement path; our onboarding cadence is driven by the package level (pilot vs production commitment). Marketplace purchases can access standard support tiers; enterprise contracts can include a named CS contact and SLA addendum.

4) Compliance & MSA: For SOC 2 and data residency addenda we typically execute a direct MSA with an attached vendor security addendum. If you prefer marketplace, we can still sign a supplemental security addendum and attach it to purchase documentation — procurement simply needs to accept the supplemental in writing.

Suggested next steps: confirm call Thursday 11/4 10:00am PT, Redwood prepares a 1-page MAP and a sample order form + MSA highlight sheet. I've attached a MAP draft (Horizon-MAP-draft.xlsx) and a highlighted MSA extract.
